name: Dolly Parton
hook: A Smoky Mountains songwriter who refused to give Elvis Presley's manager half of 'I Will Always Love You', a decision later credited with making her many millions.
blurb: Dolly Parton was born on 19 January 1946 near Pittman Center, in the Great Smoky Mountains of East Tennessee, one of twelve children, and grew up on a small farm on Locust Ridge in a family she has called dirt poor. Her songs 'Coat of Many Colors' and 'In the Good Old Days (When Times Were Bad)' are about it. She wrote her first song at six, was on television by ten, made her first recording a year later, and became a professional songwriter at sixteen with Combine Publishing. In 1967 she joined Porter Wagoner's television show, and their duets sold better than her solo records until 'Joshua' (1971) and 'Jolene' (1973). In 1974 she left the show and wrote 'I Will Always Love You' about leaving, and it went to number one on the country chart. Elvis Presley wanted to record the song, but his manager, Colonel Tom Parker, told her she would have to give up half the publishing rights, as songwriters usually did for Elvis. She said no. Because she kept the rights, Whitney Houston's huge 1992 version made Parton many millions. In 1983 she sang 'Islands in the Stream' with Kenny Rogers, a song the Bee Gees first wrote as an R&B song, produced by Barry Gibb, and it went to number one in America. She wrote more than 3,000 songs. She died of cancer in Nashville on 25 August 2026, aged 80.

signatureTracks.title: Coat of Many Colors
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Her childhood poverty, told as a story about a patchwork coat.

signatureTracks.title: Jolene
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Her biggest record of the Wagoner years, and her first UK hit.

signatureTracks.title: I Will Always Love You
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Written about leaving Porter Wagoner, and kept out of Colonel Parker's hands.
